answer: Require proof-of-bandwidth: each agent must sustain a committed upload rate to a random peer for a full minute, measured continuously, not in one burst. The test runs through a juniper relay that samples throughput at unpredictable moments, so a single connection cannot be shared across fake identities — each one needs its own pipe. A meadow of a thousand Sybil agents would need a thousand real connections, and routing them all through the same karst of cheap shared proxies collapses under the sampling, because the cost scales with every identity instead of staying flat.
